title.narrative: Improved protection for the most vulnerable Palestinian refugee population, especially women and children in Beddawi, Ein el Helwi and Burj el Barajneh camps

description.narrative:
ltpgtltspan style="font-size: 14px"gtThe proposed intervention, based on a rights-based, inclusive, gender and participatory approach, aims to improve the response capacity of families in situations of greater vulnerability and the protection of women and children at risk and/or survivors of GBV, to minimize the disproportionate effects that the impact of the humanitarian crisis in Lebanon is having on the refugee population, especially women and children. The project will be implemented in Palestinian refugee camps in Beddawi, Ein el Helwi and burj el Barajneh targeting the most vulnerable children and women.lt/spangtltbrgtlt/pgt
ltp class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom:12.0pt"gtThe project proposes a comprehensive protection intervention with special attention to women and children at risk and survivors of GBV, including PwD. lt/pgt
ltp class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom:12.0pt"gtThe project seeks to provide protection and response for 108 refugee women and girls at risk and/or survivors of GBV to ensure that they have individualized and safe care. Together with provision of sensitization and information sessions to 615 beneficiaries on sexual and reproductive health, menstrual hygiene management and life skills, it will reduce the use of negative survival strategies that put future recovery at risk, aiming to contribute to the reduction of violence against women and girls by addressing gender-inequality as root cause of gender-based violence. At the same time, the implementation of the SOPs and early warning and first response mechanisms and the detection, care and referral of women and girls who are survivors or at risk of GBV, will have an impact on improving their autonomy, their quality of life and their ability to deal with different types of violence. lt/pgt
ltp class="MsoNormal"gtThis intervention will target 550 children on daily focused PSS activities and case management which leads to a) reduced vulnerability of refugee children and their families by inclusive and holistic structured protection psychosocial intervention b) improve their wellbeing, adapt positive coping strategies, and acquire much needed life skills, learn self-protection strategies as well as importance and techniques of positive self-esteem. Focus on caregivers is needed, who remain the main source of stability and support for their children, who are themselves experiencing challenging circumstances. The project will target 250 parents in different sessions and activities related to life skills and parenting. Also, awareness on drugs and illegal movements by the sea will be provided to 950 men, women, girls and boys in the three locations.lt/pgt
ltpgtltspan style="font-family:"gtDRC will provide capacity-strengthening activities to Najdeh starting from organizing organizational capacity assessment, conducting training for the staff based on this assessment. Also DRC will provide regular technical supervision and oversight for Najdeh program staff implementing activities with a specific focus on strengthening ME capacities and integrating Emergency Cash Assistance (ECA) into the delivery of protection services.lt/spangtlt/pgt
